text.content:
Keeps & Kingdoms, a companion for The Arneyan Codex. Version 0.5.0.

Rules to read and run by hand: strongholds and followers, warfare, domains and intrigue, and monsters. The creatures are actors in the Keeps & Kingdoms: Monsters compendium.

Adapted for home play from MCDM's Strongholds & Followers, Kingdoms & Warfare, Flee, Mortals! and Where Evil Lives, rewritten for The Arneyan Codex. Not an MCDM product, and not for sale or distribution.

• What it is: a stronghold is a place of your own, a keep, a tower, a temple or a house of secrets, that gives you powers no level does.
  • What owning one does:
    • It improves your class's signature feature (Strongholds by Class).
    • It draws followers to you.
    • It ties you to the land around it, your demesne.
  • When: there's no Level requirement; gold is the gate. Most parties can afford one in the Heroes of the Realm tier (5 to 10). By Masters of the Realm (11 to 16), "you command respect, armies and fortresses".
  • Optional rules. Strongholds are for tables that want them; the GM decides whether they're in play.

StrongholdForVariants
KeepRaising units, defending the land, arms trainingBarbarian Camp (moves), Pirate Ship (sails)
TowerRefining spells, battle magicTower by school
TempleCalling servitors from your godDruid Grove
EstablishmentIncome, rumours, intelligence, favours(sits inside a town)
CastleTwo or more of the above in one place(see Other ways to get one)
  • Anyone can build any type. A fighter with a tower needs a caster friend to get much from it.

  • Stronghold level: 1st to 5th. Building straight to a higher level costs the same as building and then upgrading.
  • No rushing: the times assume a good crew. More hands only get in each other's way.
  • The GM's dial: scarce labour, poor stone or a recent war can raise the cost or the time; plentiful iron or grateful locals can lower them.
  • Fortifications: in a battle (Chapter 4), a stronghold fights as one of the fortifications there, growing as it is upgraded.
Stronghold1st–2nd3rd–4th5th
KeepKeepCastleCastle, +2 HP
Tower or TempleTowerTower, +2 HPKeep
Establishmentnonenonenone

• Castles.
    • Cost: add up the cost and time of each type it holds, then add 10% per type. A keep, tower and temple together cost 3,380 gp and take 507 days.
    • No doubles: a castle can't hold two of the same type.
    • Who benefits: each type's benefit serves one character at a time.
  • Ruins.
    • Base cost: clear out a ruin and rebuild it for half the cost and half the time.
    • Savings: each floor with some rooms still standing saves a further 50 gp and 7 days; each floor wholly intact saves 100 gp and 14 days.
    • Size: a big ruin may come back as a 2nd- or 3rd-level stronghold, never higher.
  • Grants.
    • How: a lord may reward a great deed with a title and a stronghold.
    • The catch: there's always a cost, whether repairs, the monsters still inside, or the debt to the lord.
    • Who holds it: one character is the named holder, even when the whole party lives there.

• The master: whoever paid for it. The master decides who uses its benefits.
  • One at a time:
    • Each benefit serves one character at a time.
    • Each character uses one stronghold benefit at a time.
    • Switching takes an Extended Rest.
  • Demesne: your demesne reaches 4 hexes per stronghold level around it.
    • You sense when the land is sick or wronged.
    • The powers come from your bond with it.
    • If a lord abuses them, the land's patience runs out (GM's call).
  • Stronghold actions and demesne effects (Strongholds by Class):
    • They work inside the stronghold unless they say otherwise.
    • Their DC is your Class Save DC, or your Spell Save DC for a caster's.
  • Upkeep: there is none for the building. You pay for units (Warfare), and the demesne's taxes cover the stronghold's own (Chapter 5). The Knight still pays his Call-to-Arms followers. Everyone else lives off the demesne.
  • Neglect: a stronghold left for about a year becomes a ruin. A druid grove left untended for a month goes wild (see The Druid Grove).
  • Enemies: a new keep is a threat to every lord around it. Start with three neighbours: an enemy, a weaker but wiser ally, and a neutral party who could tip the balance.
  • Optional: a stronghold gives no benefit until you have held it against one attack.

• What it is: a downtime week spent at your stronghold, seeing to your people. It can be the same week as a downtime course you take there.
  • What it refreshes: every power that says "per Extended Rest": class feature improvements, refined spell casts, school days, the library's uses and the tailor's uses.
  • What you can change: your keep training, which castle benefit you use, and (multiclass) which class feature your stronghold improves.
  • At your own temple: an Extended Rest also clears your Petition Strain (see The Temple).

People know it's there

  • Hundreds of workers for months: a keep can't be built in secret without magic.
  • A player who tries finds the hiding causes its own trouble.

Raising units

  • When it's finished: you gain 2 + keep level units (Warfare).
    • Optional pacing: one unit when work starts, one halfway, and the rest on completion.
  • New units: each is Size 1d4 and of your people. Rolling the same unit again raises its Size to 1d6 rather than adding a second one.
  • Buying more: mercenary units can be bought (Warfare). A keep cuts unit cost and upkeep by 10% per level.

Units raised by a keep (d20)

d20Unitd20Unit
1–4Green light infantry15Seasoned medium or heavy infantry
5–8Green medium infantry16–17Green archers (light or medium)
9–11Regular light infantry18Regular archers
12–14Regular medium infantry19Regular cavalry (light or medium)
20Seasoned light cavalry

Training

  • The rule: choose one, always on, while you hold the keep. You must be trained in the weapon or armour. You can change it on an Extended Rest.
TrainingEffect
Light ArmourAdvantage on Tumbling and balance checks while in light armour
Medium Armour+5ft speed in medium armour
Heavy ArmourRanged attacks against you have Disadvantage while you're in heavy armour
ShieldWhen you hit with a weapon while holding a shield, push the target 5ft
BludgeoningOn a critical hit, the target has Disadvantage on attacks and saves until the start of your next turn
Piercing+1d6 damage against a creature in heavy armour (or natural armour as hard, GM's call)
Slashing+1d6 damage against a creature in light armour or none
ReachWhen you hit with a reach weapon, move the target 5ft; it must stay within your reach
VersatileWhile you wield a versatile weapon in two hands, reroll 1s on its damage dice
FinesseOnce per round, out of turn, when a creature within 5ft hits you in melee, make one melee attack against it with a finesse weapon (a Swashbuckler instead gains one extra Riposte each round)

Barbarian Camp (a keep on the move)

  • Cost: half a keep's.
  • Units: light units only. Roll on the keep table and turn any medium or heavy result into light.
  • Discount: there's no unit discount.
  • Movement: each season it can move 4 hexes × (6 − its level): 20 hexes at 1st, 4 at 5th.
  • Raiding: a season camped in settled land is a raid, and the lords there will answer it (Chapter 5).
  • Other uses: the same rules suit any host that travels, such as a druid's walking trees or a monk's peasant uprising.

Pirate Ship (a keep at sea)

  • Units: raised like a keep's, none bigger than Size 1d6. It carries as many units as its level.
  • The ship: a sailing ship, longship, galley or warship from the Shopkeeper's Catalogue. Its Catalogue price is its build cost, in place of a keep's.
  • Speed: its Catalogue speed, +1 hex a day per ship level.
  • Plunder: a week in port earns 10 gp. Winning a battle against a port town plunders it (Chapter 5).
  • Ship rules: sailing, crews, weather and ship combat are in Ships & Sea Travel in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue.

Spell refinement

  • What it is: at your tower you can take a spell you know and refine it, adding a rider from the tables below.
    • The refined spell is a new spell, one level higher, and it takes your name. Naming a spell is the oldest ambition in the trade.
    • It sits on top of the Handbook's Research a Spell.
  • Which spells: any spell you can cast that doesn't already carry a maker's name. A cantrip becomes a 1st-level spell.
  • Time: 4 weeks, +1 week per spell level, −1 week per tower level (minimum 1 week). You must work without a break.
  • Cost: 10 gp per spell level, for materials.
  • Choosing the rider: decide which table fits the spell's targets (you or one ally; several allies; one enemy; several enemies; or a damage spell, by damage type). Then roll d8, or the GM and player pick together.
  • Limits:
    • You know refined spells up to your tower level.
    • Each spell can be refined once.
    • You can refine a spell one level above what you can cast now; it works once you reach that level.
  • Casting it:
    • You can cast each refined spell a number of times equal to your casting modifier (minimum 1) per Extended Rest.
    • If the target saves, the rider fails.
    • You have Advantage on saves against your own refined spell.
    • Once it settles, you may teach it.

You or one ally (d8)

  • Empowering: one random attribute becomes 20 for 10 minutes (if it was lower).
  • Regenerating: regain HP equal to your casting modifier at the start of each of its turns while the spell lasts.
  • Mindful: it uses your casting modifier for all saves for 10 minutes.
  • Third Eye: it sees hidden, disguised and invisible creatures within 60ft for 10 minutes.
  • Levitating: it gains a fly speed of 10ft for 10 minutes.
  • Invulnerable: it takes no damage until the end of its next turn.
  • Shifting: for 10 minutes, at the start of each of its turns, on a d6 roll of 4+ it may teleport 10ft.
  • Blazing: until the end of its next turn it leaves a trail of fire. Anyone who enters it or starts there takes 3d6 fire (Reflex half).

Several allies (d8)

  • Fleet: +10ft speed and no difficult terrain for 10 minutes.
  • Hastening: each may move half its speed before acting, for 10 minutes.
  • Energising: until the end of their next turn they have Advantage on attack rolls, and creatures have Disadvantage on saves against their spells.
  • Oracular: they see magic items and lasting spells within 60ft for 10 minutes. A Hard Spellcraft check names one.
  • Fated: each may reroll its damage dice once until the end of its next turn.
  • Vengeful: for 10 minutes, once per round, out of turn, each may attack a creature that hits it.
  • Revealing: their Perception checks count as a 20 until the end of their next turn.
  • Gloating: for 10 minutes, dropping an enemy to 0 HP grants a free move of half speed or one more attack (at Disadvantage, like any extra attack).

One enemy (d8)

  • Betraying: it makes one attack against a target you choose.
  • Beguiling: until the end of your next turn it doesn't see you as an enemy; you have Advantage on attacks against it, and it has Disadvantage on saves against your spells.
  • Distracting: on its next turn it can move or act, not both.
  • Elucidating: it blurts out a secret.
  • Stupefying: its Intelligence is 3 until the end of its next turn.
  • Illuminating: it glows until the end of its next turn. Attacks against it have Advantage, and it shows up hidden creatures beside it.
  • Confusing: its next attack goes at a random creature it can reach, and it moves towards that creature.
  • Exposing: its armour and clothes vanish until the end of its next turn (AC 10 + Dexterity).

Several enemies (d8)

  • Overwhelming: knocked Prone.
  • Thunderous: pushed 10ft.
  • Defiling: 1d6 necrotic each; you gain temporary HP equal to the total.
  • Rooting: they can't move until the end of their next turn.
  • Blinding: Blinded for 1 round per tower level.
  • Hideous: their arms become tentacles until the end of their next turn, so they drop what they hold. A creature with no arms grows them and its attacks and spells fail.
  • Enfeebling: Vulnerable to fire, cold, lightning or acid (your choice each casting) for 1 round per tower level.
  • Telekinetic: all moved 10ft the same way. If lifted, each takes 1d6 on landing and makes a Moderate Tumbling check or falls Prone.

Damage spells (by damage type, no roll)

TypeRider
Acid, MeltingIts carried gear takes the spell's damage too
Bludgeoning, SunderingAttacks against it have Advantage while the spell lasts
Cold, ChillingIt can't move until the end of its next turn
Fire, BurningBurning 1 (Handbook conditions)
Force, FellingProne, and it can't stand on its next turn
Lightning, ShockingDisadvantage on saves until the end of your next turn
Necrotic, UnholyOne ghoul rises within 30ft and obeys you for rounds equal to your casting modifier; it counts as your one spell-made attacker
Piercing, PuncturingWeapon attacks against it crit on 18–20 for 10 minutes
Poison, NauseatingIt loses its next turn
Psychic, MaddeningOn its next turn it treats friends as foes and foes as friends
Radiant, DazzlingBlinded until the end of its next turn
Slashing, WoundingIt takes 1d10 more at the end of its next turn
Thunder, ConcussivePushed 20ft

Tower by school (instead of refinement, or as well if the GM allows)

  • The dedication: dedicate your tower to one school of magic.
  • The benefit: after an Extended Rest there, you cast spells of that school at +2 caster level for a number of days equal to tower level.

Petitioning your god

  • Who: anyone can petition their god. A temple you own makes it far likelier to work.
  • How:
    • The roll: it takes your action. The GM rolls d100 + your Level + 30 if you own a temple + 20 if you are Favoured (Strained +0) − your Petition Strain.
    • Forsaken: you can't petition.
    • Without Divine Favour: only Clerics, Paladins and Battle Priests have Divine Favour; anyone else adds +0.
  • Petition Strain:
    • Every petition adds the strain in the last column, whatever the result.
    • It stacks, and an Extended Rest at your own temple clears it.
RollResultStrain
1–20Rebuked: Disadvantage on attacks and saves for 1 minute+20
21–65Unheard+15
66–75Blessed: Advantage on saves and your first attack each round for 1 minute+10
76–84Type I servitor+10
85–94Type II servitor+10
95–104Type III servitor+15
105–109Type IV servitor+20
110–114Type V servitor+25
115+Type VI servitor+30

Servitors

  • Choosing: choose a servitor of the Type you rolled from your god's row below. It must suit your god's nature, and the GM must agree.
  • Duration: it stays 4 rounds + 1 per stronghold level and fights for you.
  • Death: if slain, it leaves its body and returns home.
  • Limits: a servitor is a god's gift, not a spell, so it doesn't count as your one spell-made attacker. A servitor never uses solo rules: one action a round, no villain actions.

Servitors by power

  • Celestial (good gods): I Pegasus (4); II Unicorn (7); III Couatl (9); IV Deva (10); V two Devas; VI Planetar (15).
  • Devils (lawful evil): I two Bearded Devils (3); II Chain Devil (7); III Barbed Devil (8); IV Bone Devil (8) and two Bearded Devils; V Ice Devil (12); VI Horned Devil (12) and an Erinyes (7).
  • Demons (chaotic evil): I Shadow Demon (5); II two Shadow Demons; III Hezrou (8); IV Vrock (11); V Glabrezu (11) and a Shadow Demon; VI Nalfeshnee (13).
  • Yugoloths (neutral evil): I Mezzoloth (5); II two Mezzoloths; III three Mezzoloths; IV Nycaloth (10); V Ultroloth (13); VI Arcanaloth (15).
  • Elementals (nature and elemental gods): I Gargoyle (5); II Fire Elemental or Invisible Stalker (7); III Salamander (8); IV Air, Earth or Water Elemental (10); V Efreeti (12), or a Djinni (10) and an Elemental; VI two Elementals (10).
  • Undead (death gods): I Wraith (5); II Wight (6); III Mummy (8) or Ghost (9); IV a Ghost and two Ghasts (5); V a Ghost, a Wight and a Wraith; VI a Ghost, two Wights and two Ghasts.
  • Levels: each creature's Level is shown in brackets, from Monsters & Treasure.

• No temple bonus: a grove doesn't give the +30. The druid can still petition without it.
  • Installing a spell:
    • Spend a month in meditation there, and if the powers agree, one spell from the list is installed in the grove for good.
    • The druid casts it there even if it isn't a druid spell they know. Each casting pays the spell's material cost.
SpellHow often
ReincarnateOnce per season
ForesightOnce per season
Greater RestorationOnce per month
HealOnce per month
ResurrectionOnce per year
  • Tending: someone must tend the grove: the druid, a lieutenant or a follower. A month untended and it goes wild, and the spell is lost.

• Income: 100 gp per level each season (13 weeks). It can pay for castle upgrades.
  • Rumours:
    • Before or during an adventure, pay 10 gp × level, then make a Gather Information check (GM's DC).
    • On a success, you learn one kind of creature you'll face and roughly how many. You have Advantage on attacks against them a number of times equal to your establishment level.
    • The GM may add one hint: a secret door or way out, a trap, a riddle, or a powerful item.
  • Gather Information:
    • The roll: d20 + your Charisma modifier + a bought bonus (+1 per 10 gp, at least 10 gp, up to your establishment level).
    • DC: Moderate for big, open groups; Hard for secretive ones; Severe for those that guard against spies. Name a hidden inner circle before you roll; it's harder.
    • Limits: checks per season equal your level, and only one per group each season.
    • Reach: 4 hexes per level.
    • What you learn: something you can act on, never a bare yes or no. It's always "a trusted employee overheard it".
  • Favours:
    • Once per season, pay 100 gp to an ally who owns a stronghold.
    • Keep favour: units for one battle (Warfare), which go home afterwards.
    • Tower favour: cast the ally's refined spell a number of times equal to your establishment level.
    • Temple favour: one petition using the ally's god and favour; the servitor stays rounds equal to your establishment level.
    • A player ally can haggle.
